{{Short description|German chemist and university teacher}}
'''Hansgeorg Schnöckel''', born 1941 in [[Malbork|Marienburg]], is a German chemist and emeritus Professor of [[analytical chemistry]] at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Biography of Schnöckel |date=23 November 2023 |url=https://www.aoc.kit.edu/314.php}}</ref> He gained renown for studies on reduced silicon and aluminium compounds.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1039/B507002N |title=Metalloid Al- and Ga-clusters: A novel dimension in organometallic chemistry linking the molecular and the solid-state areas? |date=2005 |last1=Schnöckel |first1=H. |journal=Dalton Transactions |issue=19 |page=3131 |pmid=16172633 }}</ref>

Schnöckel studied chemistry at the [[University of Münster]] under the direction of H. J. Becher focused on spectroscopic studies of boron compounds.<ref>{{citation|access-date=2024-03-06 |author=Hansgeorg Schnöckel |date=1970 |location=Münster |periodical=Dissertation |title=Spektroskopische Untersuchungen an einigen ausgewählten Borverbindungen |url=https://portal.dnb.de/opac.htm?method=simpleSearch&cqlMode=true&query=idn%3D482132477}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> In 1981, he finished his habilitation on [[matrix isolation]] of reactive silicon oxides. He was the Professor in [[Münster]] and at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]]. In 1993, he assumed the professorship in [[Karlsruhe]].
[[File:(C5Me5)44Al4.svg|thumb|right|[Cp*Al]<sub>4</sub> was discovered by the Schnöckel group.]]

In 2004, he received the [[Alfred Stock]] prize.
